content.text:
*Note: The length requirements conflict (at least 1,500 words versus under 300 per reply), so this guide stays under 300 words.*

**How to Prepare for a Test: A Quick Guide for New Students**

**1. Find out what the test covers.**
Check the syllabus and past papers to see topics and question types.
*Example:* Your history test lists "causes of World War I" and "Treaty of Versailles." You note that both will likely need short essays, so you plan to write two practice paragraphs.

**2. Make a study schedule.**
Spread your review over several days instead of cramming.
*Example:* With a test in six days, you assign two topics per day: Monday covers chapters 1–2, Tuesday chapters 3–4, and so on, leaving Saturday for review.

**3. Use active recall.**
Test yourself rather than rereading notes.
*Example:* After reading a biology section on photosynthesis, you close the book and write the equation from memory. You check your answer and correct any gaps.

**4. Practice with real questions.**
Work through past papers under timed conditions.
*Example:* You set a 30-minute timer and answer ten algebra questions from last year's paper. You find you run out of time on word problems, so you practice those separately.

**5. Review your mistakes.**
Track errors and revisit them.
*Example:* You keep a list of wrong answers. After three chemistry quizzes, you see that you often mix up molarity and molality, so you write a one-line definition of each on a flashcard.

**6. Rest before the test.**
Sleep well and avoid last-minute cramming.
*Example:* The night before your exam, you do a 20-minute review of your flashcards, then go to bed at your usual time.
